newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bosnia conference to back peace consolidation plan.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia conference to back peace consolidation plan.

text.p: Bosnia's three co-presidents and major powers will adopt a two-year peace consolidation plan for the former Yugoslav republic on Thursday after a flareup of fighting highlighted the truce fragility.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, who will co-chair the Paris meeting with international mediator Carl Bildt, said the aim was to give a new impulse to the civilian peace process a year after the Dayton accords ended the Balkans conflict.

"A number of things are still fragile. That's true for the establishment of joint institutions, which is running late...It is true of the return of refugees, which faces many problems, and it's true for reconstruction, which has barely begun," he told a news conference.

Dramatising the problems, Serbs and Moslems clashed in the disputed village of Gajevi in northeastern Bosnia on Tuesday in the worst fighting since the Dayton peace accord. American and Russian soldiers had to separate the sides after at least two Moslems were killed and several people injured.
Moslem refugees prevented from returning to their homes in Gajevi shouted insults and spat on an American officer in angry protests on Wednesday.

U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher met the three Bosnian co-presidents jointly in Paris to press home their responsibility for ensuring the peace agreement and joint institutions agreed at Dayton work in practice.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Christopher discussed with Moslem Alija Izetbegovic, Serb Momcilo Krajisnik and Croat Kresimir Zubak what he called the "very, very bad, negative incident" in Gajevi.

De Charette said the Paris conference's priorities were to complete Bosnia's institutions, build a working market economy, speed the return of refugees displaced by ethnic cleansing, and improve civil liberties, including press freedom.

A French draft of the declaration to be issued on Thursday, obtained by Reuters, contains a pledge by the co-presidents to have a working cabinet, parliament, central bank, constitutional court and military committee in place by March at the latest.

The document involves mutual commitments by the Bosnian leaders and the international community. It also includes an appeal by the Bosnian co-presidency to mantain an international military force in Bosnia after the mandate of the NATO-led Peace Implementation Force (IFOR) expires at the end of the year.

A second conference in London in December will adopt a more detailed action programme for the next year, by which time NATO is likely to have formally approved a slimmed-down peacekeeping force to succeed IFOR.
France wants the force to be gradually phased out over the two-year consolidation period, while the United States and other allies are only talking about the next 12 months.
"It is important to make sure the substance of a lasting peace is built...to give meat to the Bosnian peace," a senior U.S. official said.

He said Washington was determined to go ahead on what he called a cautious rearming of the Moslem-Croat federation in Bosnia to create a balance of power with the Serbs, whom he accused of not fully declaring their weapons.

Burns said Christopher pressed Izetbegovic again to fire Deputy Defence Minister Hasan Cengic, who Washington believes is obstructing a U.S. plan to equip and train the forces of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation.
The United States is witholding delivery of $100 million of arms until Cengic, accused of being close to Iran, is dismissed.
A senior U.S. official said Washington expected Cengic to be removed soon, as well as an unnamed Croat official who was also blocking the process of Moslem-Croat integration.

After intensive preparatory talks, Thursday's conference will be relatively brief, with a three-hour working session to approve the statement of guiding principles, a lunch and a final ceremony at President Jacques Chirac's Elysee palace.

The countries attending will be Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia and rump Yugoslavia, the United States, Russia, France, Britain, Germany, Italy, Canada, the Netherlands, Ireland as current president of the European Union and Turkey, representing the Islamic Conference Organisation.
Several international organisations will also be represented: the United Nations, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe and NATO.
